analysis.title: Tech turbulence as an opportunity: Investing selectively in the future of AI
key_insights: UBS CIO expects demand for AI infrastructure to remain strong, while investor expectations for capital discipline, monetization and balance sheet quality are rising.

The current correction in technology stocks may mark the start of a new phase in the AI cycle. Earnings growth remains strong, but investors want clearer evidence that heavy cloud and computing investment can generate lasting returns, and they are more concerned about sustainable financing and competitive pressure.

Demand for computing power continues to grow strongly. Leading US technology companies reported rapid growth in demand for AI services this earnings season, and UBS expects demand to keep rising in the coming years.

Financing risk: smaller data center providers that fund construction mainly with debt depend on customers using the new capacity. If utilization falls short, interest and principal are still due, and refinancing at higher rates adds to the burden.

At some of the major US technology companies, cash outflows now exceed revenue from existing and new AI-driven business segments. The shortfall must be covered with equity and often debt, which UBS says recalls earlier financial crises that originated in rising debt. UBS still considers an abrupt halt or substantial slowdown in the investment wave unlikely.

Business model risk: AI offerings can add revenue but can also displace existing streams. In search, an AI assistant that answers directly changes how advertising is integrated and the price paid for it, so greater usage does not necessarily raise revenue. Strong AI infrastructure demand can also raise the cost of established services.
Competition among AI model providers has increased and could intensify. Regulation can also affect the outlook.
Valuation: when investors already expect strong growth, even strong results can temporarily disappoint.

Positioning advice: keep AI exposure but diversify it. Reduce concentration risk by spreading across semiconductors, computing power, and energy and infrastructure providers. Diversification within AI is not a substitute for broad portfolio diversification.
Review portfolio weights regularly against the strategic asset allocation, and use real assets and bonds from high-quality borrowers to stabilize portfolios.

UBS sees AI exposure as worthwhile long term, particularly for investors in Switzerland and Europe, where technology stocks are scarce in home markets, subject to risk tolerance, liquidity needs and horizon.

Central message: long-term importance of AI and short-term performance of AI stocks are not the same. The next phase will reward companies that earn money consistently from AI and manage investment with discipline.

sector_views.rationale: Keep long-term AI exposure but diversify across semiconductors, computing power, and energy and infrastructure providers to reduce concentration risk.
Described as complementary building blocks that add stability to portfolios.

earnings_insights: Leading US technology companies reported rapid growth in demand for AI services in the current earnings season. The report gives no company names or figures.
Strong earnings growth continues, but investors want evidence that heavy infrastructure spending produces lasting returns.
risk_factors: Overbuilding of AI data center capacity.
Debt-financed data center providers face utilization shortfalls and refinancing at higher rates.
Cash outflows at some large US technology companies exceed AI-related revenue, requiring equity and debt funding.
AI products may displace existing revenue streams, such as search advertising.
Rising costs of established services from AI infrastructure demand.
Increasing competition among AI model providers.
Valuations already reflect optimism, so strong results can still disappoint.
vol_and_positioning: Concentration risk in AI exposure should be reduced by diversifying across semiconductors, computing power, and energy and infrastructure providers.
Expectations already priced into AI stocks mean strong results can temporarily disappoint.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand for computing power and AI services keeps growing strongly, and UBS considers an abrupt halt or substantial slowdown in investment unlikely given the size of the AI opportunity and technology companies' financial strength.
tension_points.bear_case: Cash outflows at some major US technology companies exceed AI-related revenue and are covered with equity and debt. Debt-financed smaller providers depend on utilization, and AI answers can displace existing revenue such as search advertising.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Utilization falling short of expectations at debt-financed data center providers, which would leave interest and principal payments uncovered.

theme_stances.key_argument: Demand for AI infrastructure stays strong, but investors now want evidence that heavy investment generates lasting returns and sustainable financing.
theme_stances.evidence: demand for AI infrastructure is likely to remain strong

theme_stances.key_argument: Investors should keep AI exposure but diversify it across semiconductors, computing power, and energy and infrastructure providers to reduce concentration risk.
theme_stances.evidence: investors should not abandon their AI exposure, but diversify it
